arxiv-2112-00311.title: Gravitational lens on de-Sitter background
arxiv-2112-00311.creator: Keita Takizawa, Hideki Asada
arxiv-2112-00311.description: Abstract Gravitational lenses are examined in de-Sitter (dS) background, for which the existence of the dS horizon is taken into account and hyperbolic trigonometry is used together with the hyperbolic angular diameter distance. Spherical trigonometry is used to discuss a gravitational lens in anti-de Sitter (AdS) background.

arxiv-2205-07519.title: Fair Shares: Feasibility, Domination and Incentives
arxiv-2205-07519.creator: Moshe Babaioff, Uriel Feige
arxiv-2205-07519.description: Abstract We consider fair allocation of a set ℳ {\cal{M}} of indivisible goods to n n equally-entitled agents, with no monetary transfers. Every agent i i has a valuation function v i v_{i} from some given class of valuation functions.

arxiv-2306-01447.title: Comparative study of flow fluctuations in ruptured and unruptured intracranial aneurysms: A lattice Boltzmann study
arxiv-2306-01447.creator: F. Huang, S.A. Hosseini, G. Janiga, D. Thévenin
arxiv-2306-01447.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by F. Huang, S.A. Hosseini, G. Janiga, D. Thévenin. Flow fluctuations have recently emerged as a promising hemodynamic metric for understanding the rupture risk of intracranial aneurysms. Several investigations have reported in the literature corresponding flow instabilities using established computational fluid dynamics tools. In this study, the occurrence of flow fluctuations is investigated using either Newtonian or non-Newtonian fluid models in patient-specific intracranial aneurysms using high-resolution lattice Boltzmann method simulations.

arxiv-2405-15587.title: Composed Image Retrieval for Remote Sensing
arxiv-2405-15587.description: Abstract This work introduces composed image retrieval to remote sensing. It allows to query a large image archive by image examples alternated by a textual description, enriching the descriptive power over unimodal queries, either visual or textual. Various attributes can be modified by the textual part, such as shape, color, or context.

arxiv-2409-06518.title: Questioning Internal Knowledge Structure of Large Language Models Through the Lens of the Olympic Games
arxiv-2409-06518.creator: Juhwan Choi, YoungBin Kim
arxiv-2409-06518.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have become a dominant approach in natural language processing, yet their internal knowledge structures remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we analyze the internal knowledge structures of LLMs using historical medal tallies from the Olympic Games. We task the models with providing the medal counts for each team and identifying which teams achieved specific rankings.

arxiv-2410-05834.title: On cycles in monotone grid classes of permutations
arxiv-2410-05834.creator: David Bevan, Robert Brignall, Nik Ruškuc
arxiv-2410-05834.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by David Bevan, Robert Brignall, Nik Ruškuc. We undertake a detailed investigation into the structure of permutations in monotone grid classes whose row-column graphs do not contain components with more than one cycle. Central to this investigation is a new decomposition, called the M M -sum, which generalises the well-known notions of direct sum and skew sum, and enables a deeper understanding of the structure of permutations in these grid classes.

arxiv-2503-00454.title: C 0 C^{0} -Contact Anosov flows
arxiv-2503-00454.creator: Cheikh Khoule Matheus Manso Ameth Ndiaye and Khadim War
arxiv-2503-00454.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Cheikh Khoule Matheus Manso Ameth Ndiaye and Khadim War. We prove that smooth reparametrizations of the geodesic flow on a manifold of constant negative curvature are contact Anosov flows. In particular we give a new class of exponentially mixing Anosov flows. Moreover, this introduces the notion of C 0 C^{0} -contact and we prove that the classical Gray stability theorem that is known in the smooth case fails in this setting.

arxiv-2504-04956.title: Rewind : Real-Time Egocentric Whole-Body Motion Diffusion with Exemplar-Based Identity Conditioning
arxiv-2504-04956.creator: Jihyun Lee, Weipeng Xu, Alexander Richard, Shih-En Wei, Shunsuke Saito, Shaojie Bai, Te-Li Wang, Minhyuk Sung, Tae-Kyun Kim, Jason Saragih
arxiv-2504-04956.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jihyun Lee, Weipeng Xu, Alexander Richard, Shih-En Wei, Shunsuke Saito, Shaojie Bai, Te-Li Wang, Minhyuk Sung, Tae-Kyun Kim, Jason Saragih. We present Rewind ( R eal-Time E gocentric W hole-Body Mot i o n D iffusion), a one-step diffusion model for real-time, high-fidelity human motion estimation from egocentric image inputs.

arxiv-2507-17168.title: Improving LLMs’ Generalized Reasoning Abilities by Graph Problems
arxiv-2507-17168.creator: Qifan Zhang Nuo Chen Zehua Li Miao Peng Jing Tang Jia Li
arxiv-2507-17168.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have made remarkable strides in reasoning tasks, yet their performance often falters on novel and complex problems. Domain-specific continue-pretraining (CPT) methods, such as those tailored for mathematical reasoning, have shown promise but lack transferability to broader reasoning tasks.

arxiv-2509-11520.title: Know What You Don’t Know: Selective Prediction for Early Exit DNNs Thanks: Divya Jyoti Bajpai is supported by the Prime Minister’s Research Fellowship (PMRF), Govt. of India. Manjesh K. Hanawal thanks funding support from SERB, Govt. of India, through the Core Research Grant (CRG/2022/008807) and MA
arxiv-2509-11520.creator: Divya Jyoti Bajpai and Manjesh Kumar Hanawal
arxiv-2509-11520.description: Abstract Inference latency and trustworthiness of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are the bottlenecks in deploying them in critical applications like sensitive tasks. Early Exit (EE) DNNs overcome the latency issues by allowing samples to exit from intermediary layers if they attain ‘high’ confidence scores on the predicted class.

arxiv-2510-24786.title: DNN-based Signal Processing for Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers
arxiv-2510-24786.creator: Avinay Bhat, Mun Jung Jung, Gray Putnam, Haiwang Yu
arxiv-2510-24786.description: Abstract We investigate a deep learning-based signal processing for liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs), a leading detector technology in neutrino physics. Identifying regions of interest (ROIs) in LArTPCs is challenging due to signal cancellation from bipolar responses and various detector effects observed in real data. We approach ROI identification as an image segmentation task, and employ a U-ResNet architecture.

pmc-10570328.title: Macrophage CARD9 mediates cardiac injury following myocardial infarction through regulation of lipocalin 2 expression
pmc-10570328.creator: Yan Liu, Yi-hui Shao, Jun-meng Zhang, Ying Wang, Mei Zhou, Hui-qin Li, Cong-cong Zhang, Pei-jie Yu, Shi-juan Gao, Xue-rui Wang, Li-xin Jia, Chun-mei Piao, Jie Du, Yu-lin Li
pmc-10570328.description: Immune cell infiltration in response to myocyte death regulates extracellular matrix remodeling and scar formation after myocardial infarction (MI). Caspase-recruitment domain family member 9 (CARD9) acts as an adapter that mediates the transduction of pro-inflammatory signaling cascades in innate immunity; however, its role in cardiac injury and repair post-MI remains unclear.

pmc-11462149.title: High accuracy meets high throughput for near full-length 16S ribosomal RNA amplicon sequencing on the Nanopore platform
pmc-11462149.creator: Xuan Lin, Katherine Waring, Hans Ghezzi, Carolina Tropini, John Tyson, Ryan M Ziels
pmc-11462149.description: Small subunit (SSU) ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene amplicon sequencing is a foundational method in microbial ecology. Currently, short-read platforms are commonly employed for high-throughput applications of SSU rRNA amplicon sequencing, but at the cost of poor taxonomic classification due to limited fragment lengths.

pmc-12404245.title: Sex differences in the redox response to fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) air pollution protects female mice against metabolic and cardiac injury
pmc-12404245.creator: Michael Kitching, Amanda Ribble, Ashley Wright, Aruni Bhatnagar, Petra Haberzettl
pmc-12404245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure increases the cardiometabolic disease risk. While there is extensive research on how PM2.5 impairs cardiometabolic health in male mice, its health impact is largely unexplored in females. To examine PM2.5‐induced cardiometabolic effects in females, female and male mice (n = 10/group) on a regular (12 h:12 h, RLC) or disturbed (18 h:6 h, DLC) light–dark cycle were exposed to concentrated ambient PM2.5 (CAP) for 30 days.

pmc-12432464.title: A Mobile App (CareFit) Supporting Physical Activity for Informal Carers of People With Dementia: Mixed Methods Feasibility and Adaptation Study
pmc-12432464.creator: Kieren J Egan, William Hodgson, Bradley Macdonald, Ramsay Meiklem, Ryan Innes, Alison Kirk, Barbara Fawcett, Mark D Dunlop, Roma Maguire, Greg Flynn, Joshua Stott, Gill Windle, Gianpiero Greco, Jaheeda Gangannagaripalli, Sara Guerra
pmc-12432464.description: BackgroundInformal carers are critical in looking after people with dementia. The value of all informal care as a total in the United Kingdom is now estimated to be £184 billion (US $249 billion). However, many carer groups are inadequately supported and face poor mental and physical health with limited opportunities for physical activity.

pmc-13334761.title: Biological and Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Postoperative Complications Affecting Long-Term Survival: A Narrative Review
pmc-13334761.creator: Laurence Weinberg, Junyan Zhao, Luca Petterlin, Emasha Seneviratne, Rebecca Wang, Jemin Suh, Parthiv Gaykar, Tareeque Knight, Warren Lee, Dong-Kyu Lee, Nattaya Raykateeraroj
pmc-13334761.description: Postoperative complications are common after major surgery and are consistently associated with poorer long-term survival, yet the biological mechanisms underpinning this relationship remain incompletely understood. This narrative review aimed to synthesise clinical and mechanistic evidence linking postoperative complications to long-term mortality and major adverse outcomes.

pmc-13365293.title: Molecular characterization of extended-spectrum β-lactamases-producing Escherichia coli isolated from patients with bacteremia

In view of the above, our objective was to determine the antimicrobial resistance profile of 60 E.

pmc-13418630.title: Redefining the applications of navigation in spine surgery
pmc-13418630.creator: Daniel Faraj, Michael Galgano
pmc-13418630.description: Intraoperative navigation in spine surgery has evolved into an increasingly versatile platform that enhances precision, safety, and operative workflow across a variety of surgical procedures. In the setting of burst fractures, it improves spatial awareness during vertebrectomy, ensuring complete disc removal, accurate endplate preparation, and safe anterior column reconstruction.
